38 /**
39 * @brief Fortran/Column-major stride order.
40 * @details The first dimension varies the fastest, the last dimension the slowest.
41 * @tparam Rank Number of dimensions.
42 */
43 template <int Rank>
44 constexpr uint64_t Fortran_stride_order = nda::encode(nda::permutations::reverse_identity<Rank>());
45
46 /**
47 * @brief C/Row-major stride order.
48 * @details The last dimension varies the fastest, the first dimension the slowest.
49 * @tparam Rank Number of dimensions.
50 */
51 template <int Rank>
52 constexpr uint64_t C_stride_order = nda::encode(nda::permutations::identity<Rank>());

54 /**
55 * @brief Layout that specifies how to map multi-dimensional indices to a linear/flat index.
56 *
57 * @details It stores the shape of the array, i.e. the length of each dimension, and the strides of each dimension.
58 * The stride of dimension `i` is the number of elements to skip in memory when the index of dimension `i` is
59 * incremented by one. For example:
60 * - To iterate over every element of a 5x5x5 array in C-order use the strides `(25, 5, 1)`.
61 * - To iterate over every 2nd element of a 1D array use the stride `(2)`.
62 * - To iterate over every 2nd column of a 10x10 array in Fortran-order use the strides `(1, 20)`.
63 * - To iterate over every 2nd row of a 10x10 array in Fortran-order use the strides `(2, 10)`.
64 *
65 * The template parameters `StaticExtents` and `StrideOrder` are encoded as `uint64_t`. They can be decoded to a
66 * `std::array<int, Rank>` using the nda::decode function. The encoding limits the number of dimensions, i.e. the
67 * rank, to 16.
68 *
69 * The static extent array specifies the length of each dimension at compile-time. A zero value means that the length
70 * in this dimension is dynamic and will be specified at runtime. Note that static lengths cannot exceed 16 (due to
71 * the encoding). For example:
72 * - `StaticExtents = nda::encode(std::array<int, Rank>{0, 10, 0, 5})` corresponds to a 4D array with dynamic extents
73 * in dimension 0 and 2, and static extents of length 10 and 5 in dimension 1 and 3, respectively.
74 *
75 * The stride order specifies the order in which the dimensions are stored in memory. In its array form, it can be any
76 * permutation of the integer values from `0` to `Rank - 1`. The slowest varying dimension is the first element of the
77 * array and the fastest varying dimension is the last element of the array. For example:
78 * - C-order: `StrideOrder = nda::encode(std::array<int, Rank>{0, 1, ..., Rank - 2, Rank - 1})`.
79 * - Fortran-order: `StrideOrder = nda::encode(std::array<int, Rank>{Rank - 1, Rank - 2, ..., 1, 0})`.
80 *
81 * `LayoutProp` is an enum flag that can be used to make further compile-time guarantees about the layout of the data
82 * in memory (see nda::layout_prop_e).
83 *
84 * @tparam Rank Number of dimensions.
85 * @tparam StaticExtent Compile-time known shape (zero if fully dynamic).
86 * @tparam StrideOrder Order in which the dimensions are stored in memory.
87 * @tparam LayoutProp Compile-time guarantees about the layout of the data in memory.
88 */
89 template <int Rank, uint64_t StaticExtents, uint64_t StrideOrder, layout_prop_e LayoutProp>
90 class idx_map {

94 // Extents of all dimensions (the shape of the map).

96
97 // Strides of all dimensions.
98 std::array<long, Rank> str{};
99

104 /// Decoded static extents.

106
107 /// Decoded stride order.

109
110 /// Encoded stride order.

113 /// Compile-time memory layout properties.

388 /**
389 * @brief Construct a new map from an array with its dynamic extents.
390 *
391 * @details The missing extents are taken from the static extents, i.e. if a static extent is zero, it is replaced
392 * by the corresponding dynamic extent.
393 *
394 * @param shape std::array with the dynamic extents only.
395 */
396 idx_map(std::array<long, n_dynamic_extents> const &shape) noexcept
397 requires((n_dynamic_extents != Rank) and (n_dynamic_extents != 0))
398 : idx_map(merge_static_and_dynamic_extents(shape)) {}
399
400 /**
401 * @brief Construct a new map from an existing map with a different stride order.
402 *
403 * @warning This constructor is deleted.
404 *
405 * @tparam SE Static extents of the other nda::idx_map.
406 * @tparam SO Stride order of the other nda::idx_map.
407 * @tparam LP Layout properties of the other nda::idx_map.
408 */
409 template <uint64_t SE, uint64_t SO, layout_prop_e LP>
410 idx_map(idx_map<Rank, SE, SO, LP> const &)
411 requires(stride_order_encoded != SO)
412 {
413 static_assert((stride_order_encoded == SO), "Error in nda::idx_map: Incompatible stride orders");
414 }
415
416 /**
417 * @brief Construct a new map with a shape of a different rank.
418 * @warning This constructor is deleted.
419 * @tparam R Rank of the given shape.
420 */
421 template <int R>
422 idx_map(std::array<long, R> const &)
423 requires(R != Rank)
424 {
425 static_assert(R == Rank, "Error in nda::idx_map: Incompatible ranks");
426 }
427
428 /// Default copy constructor.
429 idx_map(idx_map const &) = default;
430
431 /// Default move constructor.
432 idx_map(idx_map &&) = default;
433
434 /// Default copy assignment operator.
435 idx_map &operator=(idx_map const &) = default;
436
437 /// Default move assignment operator.
438 idx_map &operator=(idx_map &&) = default;
439
440 private:
441 // Get the contribution to the linear index in case of an nda::ellipsis argument.
442 template <bool skip_stride, auto I>
443 [[nodiscard]] FORCEINLINE long myget(ellipsis) const noexcept {
444 // nda::ellipsis are skipped and do not contribute to the linear index
445 return 0;
446 }
447
448 // Get the contribution to the linear index in case of a long argument.
449 template <bool skip_stride, auto I>
450 [[nodiscard]] FORCEINLINE long myget(long arg) const noexcept {
451 if constexpr (skip_stride and (I == stride_order[Rank - 1])) {
452 // optimize for the case when the fastest varying dimension is contiguous in memory
453 60 return arg;
454 } else {
455 // otherwise multiply the argument by the stride of the current dimension
456 60 return arg * std::get<I>(str);
457 }
458 }
459
460 // Is the smallest stride equal to one, i.e. is the fastest varying dimension contiguous in memory?

581 /**
582 * @brief Create a new map by permuting the indices/dimensions of the current map with a given permutation.
583 *
584 * @details Let `A` be the current and ``A'`` the new, permuted index map. `P` is the given permutation. We define

588 * - ``A'.strides()[k] == A.strides()[P^{-1}[k]]``
589 * - The stride order of ``A'`` is the composition of `P` and the stride order of `A` (note that the stride order
590 * itself is a permutation).

601 // Note that this convention is the correct one to have a (left) action of the symmetric group on
602 // a array and it may not be completely obvious.
603 // Proof
604 // let's operate with P then Q, and denote A'' = Q A'. We want to show that A'' = (QP) A
605 // A'(i_k) = A(i_{P[k]})
606 // A''(j_k) = A'(j_{Q[k]})
607 // then i_k = j_{Q[k]} and A''(j_k) = A(i_{P[k]}) = A(j_{Q[P[k]]}) = A(j_{(QP)[k]}), q.e.d
608 //
609 // NB test will test this composition

611 //
612 // A(i_k) = sum_k i_k * S[k] (1)
613 //
614 // where S[k] denotes the strides.
615 //
616 // 1- S' : strides of A'
617 // A'(i_k) = sum_k i_{P[k]} * S[k] = sum_k i_k * S[P{^-1}[k]]
618 // so
619 // S'[k] = S[P{^-1}[k]] (2)
620 // i.e. apply (inverse(P), S) or apply_inverse directly.
621 //
622 // 2- L' : lengths of A'
623 // if L[k] is the k-th length, then because of the definition of A', i.e. A'(i_k) = A(i_{P[k]})
624 // i_q in the lhs A is at position q' such that P[q'] = q (A'(i0 i1 i2...) = A( i_P0 i_P1 i_P2....)
625 // hence L'[q] = L[q'] = L[P^{-1}[q]]
626 // same for static length
627 //
628 // 3- stride_order: denoted in this paragraph as Q (and Q' for A').
629 // by definition Q is a permutation such that Q[0] is the slowest index, Q[Rank -1] the fastest

634 // so the permutation Q' is such that P{^-1}Q' = Q or Q' = PQ (as permutation product/composition).
635 // NB : Q and P are permutations, so the operation must be a composition, not an apply (apply applies
